feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital communications, solid career progression, and credible platform/leadership experience. It reads polished and substantive, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less duplication across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear professional brand: the headline, summary, and experience align well around digital strategy, communications leadership, and platform modernization.  
- Credible progression: multiple promotions at NACo show growth, trust, and increasing scope of responsibility.  
- Good specificity: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Clarity, Power BI, and the 10,000+ page migration add credibility and technical depth.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results language: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates).  
- Reduce repetition: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement”); “front-end”/“organization-wide” hyphenation is good, but punctuation and bullet formatting in work entries should be standardized. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with tighter phrasing, one or two concrete differentiators, and less overlap with the competencies section.

- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with seniority and domain: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience in mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations.”
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs”) with a sharper value proposition tied to outcomes: cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, editorial systems, and accessible policy/technical storytelling.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in CMS and workflow design, stakeholder coordination, and translating complex policy or technical issues into clear, accessible content. Strong background in advocacy messaging, digital governance, and building scalable systems that improve publishing, collaboration, and audience engagement.”

- “Cross-channel communications,” “stakeholder coordination,” and “advocacy/policy communication” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating them elsewhere verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad or repetitive phrases with sharper, senior-level terms: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Editorial operations & governance,” “Web platform modernization,” “Analytics, insights & performance reporting.”
- Standardize style and parallel structure; use either all noun phrases or all “X & Y” constructions.
- Prioritize the most marketable, recent strengths tied to target roles: strategy, platform modernization, governance, analytics, and cross-functional leadership.
- Possible rewrite: Digital transformation strategy • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform modernization & CMS administration • Editorial operations & governance • Analytics, insights & performance reporting • Workflow & systems design • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and header language.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Data analytics & reporting” duplicate more specific Topline Skills/Technical sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance to your headline, but it reads as a task list rather than a high-impact engagement. Tighten it around scope, platform leadership, and outcomes—especially where this role extends beyond your NACo experience.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform strategy, content operations, and enterprise web improvements.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-led line: “Built cross-channel workflows, governance standards, and analytics systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Rephrase technical work to sound senior and outcome-oriented: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Add measurable outcomes if possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, publishing teams enabled, search accuracy gains, time saved, or campaign performance improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with the footer project examples; keep the CV item focused on role-level scope, and let the footer carry specific project detail.
- Avoid repeating NACo-era governance/analytics language unless this role shows a new scale, toolset, or AI/search capability.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and distinguish this role from the earlier NACo positions. Emphasize transformation, team leadership, and measurable operational improvements.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading enterprise platform modernization and audience growth.”
- Tighten the website bullet to stress outcome: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing: quantify email/social growth, video output, studio cost savings, reporting adoption, or efficiency gains from governance/planning systems.
- Combine lower-value bullets: merge analytics + governance into one operational-improvement bullet focused on better reporting, decision-making, and publishing consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may partially overlap with earlier video-production bullets; frame it here as scaling in-house capability, not routine production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more mid-level and execution-focused, with clearer scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show ownership and channel-building: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications format.”
- Add measurable/process impact if available: “Coordinated editorial calendars across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing consistency and campaign alignment.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” is too similar to the Director role’s governance/standards bullet.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive strengths rather than restating broad digital/comms terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Editorial governance and content operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector and advocacy communications,” “Audience-centered content strategy.”
- Keep parallel structure; avoid mixing nouns like “messaging” and “planning” with broader capability areas.
- Consider reducing to 4 bullets for punch if space is tight; this section works best as scannable keywords, not mini-descriptions.
- If you want more impact, swap one generic item for a differentiator tied to recent work, e.g. “AI-enabled content discovery strategy” or “Enterprise web modernization leadership.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy” also repeats elsewhere; keep it only if this audience focus is a target-role priority.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, higher-value platform leadership and modernization outcomes rather than repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters tied to recent work: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items unless job-relevant: consider removing jQuery first, and only keep SharePoint/Power Pages if targeted roles require them.
- Put the strongest, most current differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, sharpen phrasing: use “Front-end implementation” instead of listing every language in a topline section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrase verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo leadership work, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & performance optimization.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace generic phrases with sharper business-facing wording: “KPI framework development,” “executive/leadership reporting,” “SEO and digital performance analysis.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & dashboarding • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive reporting • SEO and digital performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “Leadership reporting” may overlap with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; use “executive reporting” or “decision-support reporting” for distinction.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” This section should either add specificity on level/relevance or be tightened to emphasize the most current, credible platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding light qualifiers to show depth without turning this into a duplicate skills list: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, split by proficiency/relevance: **Primary: Drupal, WordPress | Working knowledge: SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep platform names only; save implementation details for the adjacent “Coding & Technical Implementation” section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; remove one instance or make this version proficiency-based.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the enterprise focus of the CV unless it supports a recent project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation-level tools and modernize phrasing around what you actively build with now.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus toward execution: “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Integrations.”
- Use cleaner, current phrasing: “HTML/CSS” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3”; keep “JavaScript,” and only retain “jQuery” if still materially used in recent Drupal work.
- Group by function for readability: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions.”
- If possible, add evidence in recent experience instead of here, e.g., custom Drupal front-end work, deployment automation, serverless scripts, or tag management ownership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” plus “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless you want this section strictly implementation-focused.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize categories and signal implementation depth, e.g.:
- **Automation & Workflow Systems:** Airtable (workflow databases, intake/tracking systems) • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams
- Remove lower-value or older-feeling tools unless actively used recently; keep the strongest, most current platforms.
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of more tools: “process automation,” “cross-team task orchestration,” or “notification workflows.”
- Consider moving collaboration apps like Slack/Teams to a separate “Collaboration Tools” line if space allows.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap as project management tools; listing all four may feel redundant.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms to include, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength from recent roles: enterprise email operations and member communications. It should signal scale or use case, not just list tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these are the exact systems you’ve actively used; otherwise remove any weaker/older tools.
- If space allows, add light context: **Enterprise email marketing, newsletter operations and audience engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- Prioritize the most recent/most relevant platform first; if Higher Logic powered NACo’s large newsletter program, consider leading with it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; avoid repeating outcomes here unless you remove them from experience.
- “Engagement” is broad and may duplicate “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this entry is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early digital operations, and concrete outputs without repeating later leadership themes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to focus on early-career impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows spanning web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outputs: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update; coordinated day-to-day digital publishing and multimedia production.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised a digital media associate’s daily work,” if accurate.
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or early production support if that’s more accurate.
- Avoid repeating governance/operations language already used more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit:
- Lead with the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Make the first sentence more specific and active: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives that supported program development and policy communications.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer contribution such as “produced digital and multimedia content to translate research into member-facing communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, stakeholders supported, projects coordinated, or audience/use case.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item focused on research/innovation support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid broad “digital operations” language here since later roles show that progression more strongly.
